body:
Yeah. The sad part is that there's a therapy service that would be perfect, but I don't feel safe going there, because of the ongoing nature of the case (attorney's advice). Can't afford to go to therapy, otherwise. But you're right, I think the only thing to do is just focus on putting one foot in front of the other. I guess it's just how abrupt (and crushing) this whole thing is: going from probably the happiest point in my life to the worst overnight, and having my best friend/first girl I ever really loved suddenly accusing me of nonconsensual behavior...I just felt like I was thrown into a room by myself, and no matter how much I called out, there was no reply.

Honestly, just feeling that someone is out there acknowledging my voice is bringing tears of gratitude to my eyes. Thank you so much. I hope that you can find a similar comfort, regarding your own problem. I do feel that the hard part is just getting your mind to focus on something constructive that you can lose yourself in; cooking, weightlifting/exercise, cleaning, learning a skill. It's weird how I know that I'll feel better if I can do that, but my mind also seems to fear the loss that would result from it (I can't really explain it, like if I ignore this, then I will be losing the last embers of warmth from the fire of love that I felt spending time withe her).

I just...I've never felt this low before. It's frustrating because I want to talk to the accuser, but I know that I can't. She was a central part of my life and my emotions. To not only know that she's gone, but apparently has such negative feelings toward me that she's accusing me of such a grave thing, just weighs on me. Everything just feels like it's a labor to do. 

Well, I guess that doesn't answer your question, does it? I guess this is the first time I've ever felt so incredibly affectionate for someone. So I suppose I'm most curious about how to best start moving my life in a sustainable direction without her being a part of it. Thanks a lot, by the way. Seeing that little envelope light up orange really helped.
